predictions.text: Doing a 10mi long run during a week that’s only 21mi total will almost always feel like a lot. Especially if you’re newer to that distance. That’s almost 50% of your weekly mileage. If you’re new and close to half marathon distance for your long run, a long run of more than 40% is provably going to feel rough. Even if it isn’t hot. I’d consider a different training schedule for that reason. But it’s different if you aren’t comfortable getting to 30-36mpw and doing 20-24mi between the other days that aren’t your long run.
I've never seen a plan where the longest run is five weeks before the half. That seems crazy to me, but I'm also not a running coach so maybe there's a logic to the plan that is unknown to me.

You absolutely can. Make sure you’re hydrating well the days before so you go into your run hydrated, and strategically plan water to be avail about along you’re route. Have someone meet you, stash a water bottle, plan to pop into a deli mid run, plan to run by a fountain. I would do 20+ milers in New England summer heat. I’d stash a water bottle at the halfway turn around point, get it, drink it, and finish the run I am a thirsty and sweaty person, I lose more/drink more than most. It was never a problem for me. Vests just got you conditioned…. Not saying it’s bad, you do what works for you, but just saying you COULD do it without it.

I wear a running vest for longer distances because it's easier to meet my carb intake goals. I can carry more gels and use a carb drink mix. If you primarily run 5-10k, there's not a lot of need for a vest. Reflectors and lights are for safety, especially in the winter when it's dark out more. For music, Shokz bone conduction headphones are kind of the cream of the crop for running. They're open ear for safety and the design means they won't fall out of your ears. If you have a running watch like a Garmin or apple watch, you can sync the headphones directly to the watch and play music that way without having to carry a phone at all.
Not to mention they don’t slide off your face when you’re sweaty! 5 more replies

I see lots of people saying 'You don't need a vest for 5k' but it is just the easiest way to carry stuff, especially atm during winter. If I wear my vest, it has separate pockets for my keys and phone at minimum. Could wear a belt but it's easier to get my phone out of a vest if I need it and then my keys don't spring out with it! Also ATM carrying gloves and a snood, and for a group evening run tonight I also popped some tissues and a protein bar in (in case I was hungry on the way home). Could not fit that all in the belt I have and today's shorts didn't have pockets. Obviously for longer runs also having water on hand is a plus!
I do believe that is the only alternative.

A lot of Very Serious Runners don’t seem to understand something about vests: they’re fashionable to a lot of people. Yes, most people don’t NEED a vest at the local 5K, but they do offer some storage and people simply like how they look. Did I NEED an arm sleeve like Allen Iverson when I was in 6th grade, getting 5 minutes per game off the bench? Nope. But it made me feel cool. Same thing goes for vests. People like how they look wearing a vest and I say more power to them.
